speaker: therapist
text: Good morning. Come in and take a seat. How has the knee been since last week?

speaker: patient
text: Better on most days. Stairs are still the hardest part, and after a long walk it aches in the evening.

speaker: therapist
text: That fits with what we saw last time. Did you manage the exercises from the first visit?

speaker: patient
text: Some of them. Honestly, I was not sure how many to do, so I did a little of everything.

speaker: therapist
text: That's very common. Today we'll make a short, clear list, and you'll get it written down so there is no guessing.

speaker: patient
text: Good. My daughter reads English well, but I would prefer to have it in Arabic.

speaker: therapist
text: We can do that. The program will be in Arabic. Let me first check how the knee moves today.

speaker: therapist
text: Can you bend the right knee as far as is comfortable? Good. And straighten it. Any pain at the end?

speaker: patient
text: A little pulling at the front when it is fully straight, nothing sharp.

speaker: therapist
text: Fine. Now stand up from this chair without using your hands, and sit down slowly.

speaker: patient
text: Like this? It is easier than last week.

speaker: therapist
text: Much better. That will be the first exercise at home: standing up from a chair without your hands and sitting down slowly.

speaker: therapist
text: Do three sets of ten, every day.

speaker: patient
text: Three sets of ten. With a rest in between?

speaker: therapist
text: Yes, rest a little between the sets.

speaker: therapist
text: Next, the band. Sit on a chair, put the band around your right ankle, and straighten the knee slowly against it.

speaker: patient
text: The green band you gave me?

speaker: therapist
text: That one. Do three sets of twelve on the right leg, every other day.

speaker: therapist
text: And breathe out as you straighten the knee. With your blood pressure, I don't want you holding your breath.

speaker: patient
text: I take my tablets every morning. The pressure has been fine.

speaker: therapist
text: Good. Just keep breathing out on the effort.

speaker: therapist
text: Third, the stairs. At home you have stairs up to the bedroom, right?

speaker: patient
text: Yes, fourteen steps.

speaker: therapist
text: Then use the bottom step. Step up leading with your right leg, then step down. Two sets of ten, every day.

speaker: therapist
text: Always hold the stair rail when you do it.

speaker: patient
text: That is the one I feel most.

speaker: therapist
text: That's why it's on the list. It should get easier week by week.

speaker: therapist
text: Now walking. Walking is good for this knee. I'd like you to walk for twenty minutes, five days a week.

speaker: patient
text: Twenty minutes in one go? Last week I stopped after ten.

speaker: therapist
text: In one go if you can. You can walk slowly.

speaker: therapist
text: Some knee pain while walking is acceptable, as long as it has settled by the next morning.

speaker: patient
text: That is good to know. I was afraid any pain meant I was damaging the knee.

speaker: therapist
text: That's a common worry. Some pain is expected with this knee.

speaker: therapist
text: Last one, the calf. Stand facing the wall with your right leg behind you, heel on the floor, and lean forward until you feel the stretch.

speaker: therapist
text: Hold it for thirty seconds, three times, every day.

speaker: patient
text: Only the right leg?

speaker: therapist
text: Only the right.

speaker: patient
text: So, five things.

speaker: therapist
text: Five things: standing up from the chair, the band, the step, walking and the calf stretch. I'll check the written program before you leave.

speaker: patient
text: Thank you. Same time next week?

speaker: therapist
text: Same time next week. Bring the band so we can check the colour.
